doc.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Church as entertainment, religion and music; ringing the bell
summary: Church was the center of life with Sunday school, services and choir; one of his chores was ringing the church bell.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: I know this is early, but in terms of your recollection, what role did church play in your life in those early years?

Church played – church in that period played a very important part, because it was everything, really. It was your entertainment, and of course, naturally, it was your religion, and it was your music. Music was very dominant in the church with the choirs, with the different things that happened in the in the church
I’m assuming that you went to Sunday school there?

You went to Sunday school and you came back – then you went back again in the afternoon for what was B Y P U, which was – I’m trying to remember what that really meant at the time. But I remember that title. And then there was the morning service. There was morning service. There was evening – first there was a service before, for the children. Then there was the regular 11 o’clock in the morning service. Then there was that afternoon service. Then there was the night service. A lot of times children didn’t go to the night service. That was the Sunday thing. Of course there was choir practice during the week. There was a lot of different things going on.
Do you remember the name of the church.
Right off the top of my head, at this point, I don’t. I don’t remember.
We can come back to that.

But I remember that one of my chores at the church was to ring the bell. There was a bell in a bell tower. Every morning, one of the things that I had to do was to go and pull this thing. It had a big bell – clanging bell, and it would go up and down. I did that. I recall that.
